text:
On Wednesday Kyle Dubas called a press conference with nothing to announce and said the quiet part: if the Penguins keep playing like this, "the types of transactions that you see from us will be very future-oriented," per the Associated Press. Erik Karlsson, in the last year of his deal, called the speculation "pretty given." Sidney Crosby talked about trades as part of what comes with losing. Thursday's home game against St. Louis is the first since, and in a season like this one every game now gets read as evidence.

Our numbers are a little kinder than the standings. The Penguins hold 52% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) at five on five, and their finishing has cost them about six goals, so the minus-10 goal difference is worse than the play. The last five have been worse, though: 46% of the chances and a 2-3-0 record, capped by a 4-1 home loss to Ottawa. Bryan Rust is on injured reserve until about Dec. 5, and Evgeni Malkin has slid into his spot beside Crosby and Rickard Rakell, up to 19:25 a night. The goaltending is the sore spot. Arturs Silovs, projected to start, is at .855 over his last five.

St. Louis comes in off an 8-6 win over Anaheim in which Cutter Gauthier scored three goals for the Ducks, which tells you how that one went. The Blues are 3-2-0 in five and about even on the season (51% at five on five). Their edge tonight is in net: Joel Hofer is at .932 over his last five and 8.4 goals saved above expected for the season. Jordan Binnington's name, meanwhile, keeps showing up in trade rumors.

Our model has this one about as close as it gets, 3.21 to 3.20 in expected goals. Our sleeper is Blues fourth-liner Aleksanteri Kaskimaki, with 2.0 expected goals in his last 10 games and five shots from high-danger spots, 13% to score.
headline: Penguins play their first game after the Dubas talk
